guides.title: Process improvement measured with consistent rubrics
guides.concept: Improvement requires comparable measurements at two times rather than redefined criteria.
guides.prerequisites: Know the difference between a proposed order, an executed order, completed evidence and the journal's reporting scope.
guides.procedure: Step 1 — record the relevant event and timestamp without later revision. Step 2 — apply the explicit quantitative operation or classification described by the example. Step 3 — check denominator, unit, eligible records and whether the data existed at the original decision time.
guides.workedCase: FICTIONAL: A process rubric scored 6/10 before and 8/10 later under the same rubric: gain is two points, or 20 percentage points.
guides.limit: Editorially stable rubric, timing and task equivalence are required.
guides.invalidation: Do not claim the outcome if the timestamps, confirmed fills, denominator, account valuation or prior documented plan are absent. Editorially stable rubric, timing and task equivalence are required.
